conviction_note: Q3 utilisation (80%) and the Safe Notos re-rate are already public, so the release's new lines are Q3 EBITDA against an unsourced one-analyst bar, the FY26 guide (USD 50-55m; my bottom-up from the company's own utilisation and day-rate disclosures lands at or above the top, so narrowing up is plausible), Q3 cash flow, and the 2027 recontracting status of Safe Eurus and Safe Zephyrus, where nothing has been announced; these offset, so the findings sum to +0.1 and the scaled number is (2*0.52-1)*6.5 = +0.26. The size is not small: the name has fallen 22% in 60 sessions and 9.9% on 7x volume on 17 Nov with no filing to explain it, so the move is large and its sign close to a coin.

findings.finding: From the company's own pre-released Q3 utilisation (80%, four high-end units at full capacity) and the Safe Notos re-rate from USD 75k to 140k/day on 1 Sept, Q3 EBITDA comes out around USD 13-15.5m and H2 at roughly 30-35m, against the 25.5-30.5m that the FY26 guide of 50-55m implies. So the guide is more likely narrowed to the top or raised than cut.
findings.why_not_priced: Management raised the guide in August knowing the Notos rate, so part of this is in the guide already. The bottom-up is my inference from the monthly updates, not a company number. If the market priced an upgrade, the stock would not be 22% down over 60 sessions with a single analyst on it. The low end of the range allows for H2 costs I cannot see (Caledonia lay-up and reactivation prep, Boreas reimbursables at low margin).

findings.finding: Q3 cash flow should recover from Q2's USD -14.2m operating cash flow: the H1 report puts that on SPS-related payables timing and says investment will 'decrease for the remainder of the year' after the April SPSs.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 printed -14.2m operating cash flow and liquidity fell to 52.3m from 87.4m; the stock still rose 1.49% that day
findings.why_not_priced: Liquidity is the bear point on a recapitalised name (USD 20m minimum cash covenant), and a quarter of cash rebuild is not something the tape shows: the stock has fallen steadily. It is kept small because the Eurus seller's credit carries a minimum USD 7m annual repayment and yearly cash interest, whose Q3 timing is not disclosed and could absorb the improvement.

findings.finding: Safe Eurus (Petrobras contract ends H1 2027) and Safe Zephyrus (ends Sept 2027) still have no announced follow-on. Petrobras closed 2026 flotel tenders on 1 June and 24 July with margins of USD 1,000 and 500, Prosafe announced no award from either, and the Q2 deck said recent Petrobras tenders 'focused on low spec units'. The release's backlog update is therefore most likely another 'still pursuing', with a 2027 utilisation gap visible.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Safe Notos re-rate award (May 2025) and Caledonia contract (May 2026) were announced separately, not in results; the backlog-only Q3 2024 report fell 22.08%
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The 60-day fall of 22% and the 17 Nov drop of 9.9% on 7x volume look like the market discounting exactly this, which is why the size is small. The range is wide both ways: an award or LOI in the release would be a large positive, and a stated gap or lower-than-expected bids a further negative.

baseline_tension: The lean (+0.49, run-up term only, no positioning anchor) is mildly contrarian-positive after the 22% 60-day fall. My findings net to about zero: a possible guide upgrade and better cash flow on one side, a recontracting gap and a large holder selling on the other. So I neither agree with the lean nor cut against it.
